reader.requirement: For an indexed file, a READ in random access mode, and a READ of a dynamic-access file that retrieves randomly, is the format 2 READ (optional KEY IS data-name-1, INVALID KEY / NOT INVALID KEY): the compiler must accept and execute it as a random retrieval, and must not accept the format 1 phrases (NEXT, AT END, NOT AT END) on a random-access file.

edition-consulted.switches: below 2002 a dynamic-access READ writing AT END/NOT AT END without NEXT is refused (COBOL7144, the 1985 SR5); from 2002 NEXT is implied
severity seam only (error strict, warning --permissive) for the SR6 phrase screen; not edition-keyed

reader.edition-search: Read KeyedIoBinder.BindRead's kind switch (AccessMode only, no edition) and the three StatementValidation checks it calls; grepped Edition.Year in StatementValidation's READ checks.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 a dynamic READ that retrieves sequentially must write NEXT (SR5, refused otherwise), so only a READ with none of NEXT/AT END/NOT AT END is the random format 2 read; from 2002 AT END implies NEXT. The random-access screen is the same code at every edition.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f21_05 covers format 2 on random and dynamic files with KEY and INVALID KEY; g85_f21_10 covers NEXT+AT END on a random file. Not exercised: INTO on a dynamic random read followed by READ NEXT from that position, AT END alone (no NEXT) on a random file, NEXT with INVALID KEY on a random file.

reader.notes: Random-access refusals and the dynamic random/sequential split behave per the 1985 text. The COBOL1720 message at --std 85 cites §2023:14.9.30.3 SR6 rather than §1985:IX.4.5.3 SR6, a citation-only blemish that does not change the verdict.
